timeRange.note: Aptian, from the PBDB first and last appearance of P. mongoliensis (stage-level dates). Several occurrences, including the type locality in the Öösh Formation, are dated only as 'Early Cretaceous' in PBDB, so the true range may be wider. Other Psittacosaurus species span a longer interval.

lengthM.note: Museum figure for the genus, not specifically P. mongoliensis.

massKg.note: Museum figure for the genus, not specifically P. mongoliensis.

summary.en: Psittacosaurus was a small plant-eating dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Asia, around 120 million years ago. Its name means 'parrot lizard'. It belongs to the ceratopsians, the same group as horned dinosaurs like Triceratops. Fossils of P. mongoliensis include animals from juveniles to adults, so scientists have been able to work out how fast it grew.

text.en: Psittacosaurus mongoliensis was the first dinosaur to have its growth curve (body mass against age) reconstructed from bone histology. It grew faster than living reptiles but slower than most birds.

uncertain.note: PBDB dates the type locality only to the Early Cretaceous; the Aptian range rests on the better-dated occurrences.
Only genus-level museum figures (length and mass) were verified; no species-specific peer-reviewed estimate was found.

sources.title: Growth curve of Psittacosaurus mongoliensis Osborn (Ceratopsia: Psittacosauridae) inferred from long bone histology
